text: Phase Shift+J/K across parents: keep auto-scroll steady
description: Cross-parent phase moves arrived as several pushes (old parent written without the phase, new parent with it appended, then a reorder). While the phase was in no child list, getSelectedPhase fell back to index 0, so Column.vue treated the gap as navigation to entry 0 and smooth-scrolled toward the top, then back (same for every descendant column). A J/K pressed during the gap acted on entry 0. Direction for key-preserving moves was also stale. Fix: findSelectedPhaseIndex returns -1 for a missing key; getSelectedPhaseEntry/moveActivePhase/Column honor it; Column compares against the last settled selection; phase.update takes insertionIndex so movePhase is one mutation.

reflections.context: Felix reported auto-scroll going haywire after Shift+J/K phase moves across parent boundaries, and asked to question the selection model.
reflections.outcome: Root cause: per-write entity pushes expose intermediate states, and the key->index derivation silently fell back to 0 for a missing key. Fixed the fallback (explicit -1), made Column scroll only from settled selections with direction recomputed on reorders, and made cross-parent moves one mutation (phase.update insertionIndex). Backend test for insertionIndex + list-store spec for the mid-move gap added; frontend 245/245 and backend phase tests green; vue-tsc/tsc clean. Not verified visually in the live UI.
reflections.effectiveness: Fixes the reported symptom and a latent correctness bug (J/K during the gap would move entry 0). Does not restructure the model.
reflections.lesson: Derived state must represent 'missing' explicitly; a clamp-to-0 fallback turns every transient data state into a fake user action. Open follow-up (awaiting Felix): selection as one focused entry + parent-chain derivation + remembered child ids, and explicit scroll intents from actions instead of inferring navigation from state diffs.

reflections.context: Follow-up self-review of the first fix while reading Felix's notes about scrolling after phase deletion.
reflections.outcome: The first version returned -1 for any missing phase key, so a phase deleted by another client (or moved to a different column) would leave the column permanently without a selection and swallow j/k. Narrowed: -1 only while the phase still exists and no parent lists it (in transit); otherwise fall back to the first entry as before. Spec extended; 246/246 frontend tests, vue-tsc clean.
reflections.effectiveness: Closes a regression I introduced before it shipped to use.
reflections.lesson: When replacing a silent fallback with an explicit 'missing' state, enumerate every way the state can become missing (transient vs. permanent) and give the permanent ones a recovery path.

status.comment: Committed (fb3a1de by Felix, refined in 8e0d832; deletion case in child aim). Tests green. Needs Felix's live Shift+J/K check across parent boundaries.
